newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha tumbles on overnight crude losses.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha tumbles on overnight crude losses.

text.p: Naphtha prices fell sharply in afternoon trade on Tuesday, dragged down by overnight crude plunges, traders said.
Open-spec naphtha for first-half March was quoted at $242.50/243.50, compared with late Monday's levels of $248.50/249.50.
Second-half March was assessed at about $240.50/241.50 in late Tuesday trading. It was traded at $246.25 on Monday.
Inter-month naphtha spreads remained virtually unchanged, with first-half March/first-half April indicated at around plus $4.50/5.50.

In middle distillate trading, Japanese jet kerosene traders were said relaxed with most February requirements having been satisfied. With winter approaching its end, March requirements for spot jet kerosene imports would be no more than three or four cargoes, traders said.
In LSWR trading, at least 1.2 million barrels out of a total of 3.5 million barrels of Indonesia's initial allocation for January are destined for Japan, traders said.
Power firms operating nuclear plants on the Japan Sea coast said the oil spill from a Russian-registered tanker has not affected plant operations. --Tokyo Energy Desk +81-3-3432-8837
